Third, a regulatory deadline that binds tomorrow: the EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency obligations begin to apply on Sunday, August 2 — disclosure that a system is AI, machine-readable marking of synthetic audio, image, video and text, notification for emotion-recognition and biometric-categorisation deployments, deepfake disclosure with creative carve-outs, and disclosure of AI-generated text on matters of public interest absent human editorial sign-off — with one narrow grace period to December 2 this year covering only Article 50(2) marking for systems already on the market, fines to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide turnover, and the high-risk half of the same date moved out to December 2027 and August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus. Labelling, not conformity assessment, is what becomes enforceable tomorrow for anyone shipping generative output into the EU.
